title: MASCC Risk Index (Febrile Neutropenia)
aliases: Multinational Association for Supportive Care in Cancer risk index
keywords: score 21 or higher is low risk, potentially eligible for outpatient oral therapy
burden of illness none or mild is 5 points, moderate is 3, severe is 0
does not replace clinical judgment or institutional outpatient-eligibility protocol
sources: Klastersky J, Paesmans M, Rubenstein EB, et al. The Multinational Association for Supportive Care in Cancer risk index: a multinational scoring system for identifying low-risk febrile neutropenic cancer patients. J Clin Oncol. 2000;18(16):3038-3051.
IDSA has endorsed the MASCC risk index (Level B evidence) since 2002 for identifying low-risk febrile neutropenia candidates for outpatient management.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 4): the existing empiric-antibiotics-ed-icu reference covers WHICH antibiotics for febrile neutropenia but not the risk-stratification decision of admission vs. outpatient management. Burden-of-illness and hypotension point values WebSearch-verified directly against the original 2000 derivation paper; the remaining 5 components reproduced from standard knowledge, cross-checked for internal consistency against the independently-confirmed 26-point maximum (all 7 components sum to exactly 26).

purpose: Risk-stratify a febrile neutropenic cancer patient into low-risk (potential candidate for outpatient oral antibiotic therapy) versus high-risk (admission for IV antibiotics) — a distinct question from which antibiotic to choose.
notes: A score ≥ 21 identifies LOW risk for serious complications — but this alone does NOT automatically mean outpatient management is appropriate. Reliable follow-up, social support, ability to return promptly if worsening, and institutional protocol all factor into the actual disposition decision. Use this score to inform, not replace, that judgment.

items.label: Burden of febrile neutropenia (overall symptom severity)
No chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
items.help: COPD here means active disease requiring bronchodilators/steroids/oxygen or with a documented drop in FEV1 — not a remote or resolved history.

items.label: Solid tumor, OR a hematologic malignancy with no prior fungal infection

options.label: No (hematologic malignancy WITH a prior fungal infection)

items.label: Outpatient status at the onset of fever

interpretation.label: Low risk (≥ 21)
interpretation.detail: Low predicted risk of serious medical complications. A potential candidate for outpatient oral antibiotic therapy per institutional protocol, IF reliable follow-up and support are also in place — this score alone doesn't complete the disposition decision.

interpretation.label: High risk (< 21)
interpretation.detail: Higher predicted risk of serious complications — favor admission for IV antibiotics and closer monitoring.

buildNote: engine: additive, 7-item bedside score.
